summary: Regression-tested the defensive hardening changes (explicit SplashScreen control in _layout.tsx, try/catch wrapping in auth.tsx refresh()/bootstrap, AdsProvider.tsx init effect, ads.ts native module require/initialize) in the web preview. All flows pass with zero regressions: cold boot -> country select -> login (admin@reset.app) -> registration (fresh throwaway account) -> full ad-gated flow (quiz 'Pokaż moje zawody' -> rewarded-ad intro -> simulated countdown -> thanks screen -> continue -> career matches loaded). No React Native red screens, no SplashScreen/Ads/Auth related console errors or warnings observed.

react_native_issues.component: app/_layout.tsx or a screen rendered at root (pre-existing, unrelated to this session's changes)
react_native_issues.issue: Console warning seen during login/registration: 'navigation.isFocused() was called while rendering the screen __root. During render it can return a stale value...' Recommend switching to useIsFocused() hook. Not a crash, not introduced by this hardening session.

action_items: No action required for this hardening session - no regressions found in web preview.
(Pre-existing, low priority) Consider fixing navigation.isFocused() warning by using useIsFocused() hook instead of calling it during render.

Reminder: the actual native-crash-on-real-phone bug this session targeted can only be confirmed by generating a fresh Android native build (Publish) and installing on the physical device, since Expo config plugin changes (AdMob androidAppId) only take effect on a new native build, not a JS republish. This is out of scope for web/Expo Go preview testing and was correctly flagged as such in the request.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.tsx refresh(): properly nested try/catch — outer catch covers storage.secureGet failures, inner catch covers api('/auth/me') failures (incl. 401 token cleanup). Falls back to logged-out cleanly. Good.
_layout.tsx: SplashScreen.preventAutoHideAsync()/hideAsync() both wrapped in .catch(console.log) at module scope / in useEffect respectively — cannot hang or throw unhandled. Good.
AdsProvider.tsx ad-init useEffect: wrapped in try/catch, and initAds() promise itself also has .catch — double-guarded as stated. Good, no behavior change observed.

ads.ts: native module require guarded in try/catch; initialize() guarded in try/catch; adsAvailable flag correctly gates all ad calls, defaults to simulated ad in web/Expo Go. Verified functionally working end-to-end (rewarded ad flow completed during quiz 'Pokaż moje zawody').

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all requested flows passed: cold boot, login, register, ad-gated flow, console-error check)
